classification.difficultyReason: Organise marked equalities into SSS or AAS proofs with correct vertex order, then justify the target equality using corresponding elements.

content.prompt: In each part, first write a congruence statement. Then prove the required result, giving all reasons.

spec.description: Horizontally paired triangles ABC and VPT. Ordinary source blue outlines are rendered black under house style. All three distinct side-mark classes are retained.
spec.mathematics: AB=VT (two ticks), AC=VP (three ticks), BC=TP (one tick). A corresponds to V, B to T and C to P.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied vertices, edges and equality marks are visible.

answer.short: $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle VTP$ (SSS), so $\angle ACB=\angle VPT$ (matching angles of congruent triangles).
answer.worked:
$\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle VTP$ (SSS).

The marked sides give
$$\begin{align*}AB&=VT\quad\text{(given)}\\AC&=VP\quad\text{(given)}\\BC&=TP\quad\text{(given)}\end{align*}$$
Thus the triangles are congruent by SSS, with $C$ matching $P$. Therefore $\angle ACB=\angle VPT$ (matching angles of congruent triangles).

spec.description: Triangle DHF to the left of triangle TME; right-angle squares at H and M, alpha labels at F and E, and double ticks on DF and TE. Ordinary source blue outlines are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Angle DHF=angle TME=90 degrees; angle DFH=angle TEM=alpha; DF=TE. Correspondence D to T, F to E, H to M.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied vertices, right angles, alpha labels and equal-hypotenuse marks are visible.

answer.short: $\triangle DFH\equiv\triangle TEM$ (AAS), so $FH=EM$ (matching sides of congruent triangles).
answer.worked:
$\triangle DFH\equiv\triangle TEM$ (AAS).

In these triangles,
$$\begin{align*}\angle DHF&=\angle TME=90^\circ\quad\text{(given)}\\\angle DFH&=\angle TEM=\alpha\quad\text{(given)}\\DF&=TE\quad\text{(given)}\end{align*}$$
The equal sides match because they are opposite the equal right angles. Thus the triangles are congruent by AAS. Therefore $FH=EM$ (matching sides of congruent triangles).
